saferMake 1.0.0
  • Reference

    Safer-r code checks of a function

    test.Rd

    Run, in this order, the seven code checks of the safer-r project on a function, each with the dedicated function of the saferDev package:

    1. saferDev::super_assign_check(): no superassignment <<- or ->>. This check never modifies the code: it returns an error (status "error") when a superassignment is detected, because what these operators modify cannot be guessed from the code.

    2. saferDev::lambda_check(): no lambda function written \(x).

    3. saferDev::curly_bracket_check(): curly brackets { } written after if, else, for, while, repeat and function.

    4. saferDev::true_false_check(): TRUE and FALSE written in full (no T or F).

    5. saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(): a checking line of the sequence added before the for() loops whose number of iterations is not fixed by the writing itself (like 1:length(x)).

    6. saferDev::colons_check(): package attribution (<package>::) of the called functions.

    7. saferDev::all_args_here(): all the arguments of the called functions written.

    These are the checks run by the Run button of the first window of the saferMake::make() app, that calls this function.

    test(
  x,
  stop_at_first = FALSE,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

    Arguments

    x

    A function name, written without quotes and brackets.

    stop_at_first

    Single logical value. Stop at the first check that modifies the code? If FALSE (default), the checks are chained: each check is run on the function corrected by the previous checks, so that the returned function is corrected by the seven checks. Whatever this argument, the run stops at the first check that reports findings that it cannot correct itself, or that stops with an error, because the next checks can depend on these findings (e.g., saferDev::all_args_here() needs the package attributions checked by saferDev::colons_check()). If TRUE, the code returned is the one corrected by the check that stopped the run only (behavior of saferMake::make(), where the user checks the modified code before running the checks again).

    export

    Single logical value. Write the corrected function into a file? If TRUE, the file <function name>_safer.R is written in out_path (e.g., fun_safer.R for x = fun), containing an assignment of the corrected function (fun_safer <- function(...) ...), so that base::source()ing it recreates the corrected function. Nothing is exported if nothing has been corrected. An error is returned if the file already exists, and if x is not designated by a function name (like fun or package::fun).

    out_path

    Single character string indicating the path of the folder where to write the file when export = TRUE. "." (default) means the R working directory. Ignored if export = FALSE.

    safer_check

    Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

    lib_path

    Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default): only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

    error_text

    Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

    Value

    A message is always printed, with the result of each check and the reports of the saferDev functions.

    A list, returned invisibly when nothing has been corrected, made of:

    - $stage: single character string. "ok" (the seven checks report nothing), "modified" (at least one check has corrected the code, and no check reports findings), "findings" (a check reports something that it cannot correct itself, like a non basic function written without its package, or a call written on several lines for all_args_here(): the code must be completed by the user), or "error" (a saferDev function stopped with an error, which is the expected result of saferDev::super_assign_check() when a superassignment is detected). The next checks are not run after "findings" or "error".

    - $step: single integer. Number (1 to 7) of the check that stopped the run (findings, error, or modification with stop_at_first = TRUE), NULL otherwise.

    - $fun: the corrected function (with the environment of x), or NULL if nothing has been corrected.

    - $code: single character string. Code of the corrected function (starting with function), or NULL if nothing has been corrected.

    - $checks: data frame with one row per check (columns check: name of the saferDev function; status: "clean", "modified", "findings", "error" or "not run"; report: text printed by the saferDev function, or its error message).

    Details

    Requires a version of the saferDev package that provides the seven functions above (current version of saferDev, see https://github.com/safer-r/saferDev).

    Warning: saferDev::lambda_check() only sees the \(x) writing in a function carrying its source references (attribute srcref, e.g., after a base::parse(keep.source = TRUE), see the examples). The function corrected by a check is rebuilt with its source references before the next check.

    The comments and the indentation of the code are kept by the seven checks. Warning: comments are only available when x carries its source references (attribute srcref). Otherwise, the code is the deparsed one: no comments and standard indentation.

    Author

    Gael Millot

    Examples

    # Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
code1 <- "function(x){ if(x == T) sum(x) else base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \\(y){ y * 2 }) }"
fun1 <- eval(parse(text = code1, keep.source = TRUE))
res <- saferMake::test(x = fun1)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferMake::test().
#> INSIDE fun1():
#> 
#> CHECK 1/7 saferDev::super_assign_check(): CLEAN
#> CHECK 2/7 saferDev::lambda_check(): MODIFIED (the lambda functions written \(x) have been rewritten function(x).)
#> CHECK 3/7 saferDev::curly_bracket_check(): MODIFIED (curly brackets { } have been added to the bodies of the if, else, for, while, repeat and function that had none.)
#> CHECK 4/7 saferDev::true_false_check(): MODIFIED (the T and F written as values have been rewritten TRUE and FALSE.)
#> CHECK 5/7 saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(): CLEAN
#> CHECK 6/7 saferDev::colons_check(): MODIFIED (the package attribution (<package>::) of the basic R functions has been added.)
#> CHECK 7/7 saferDev::all_args_here(): MODIFIED (the missing arguments of the called functions have been added.)
#> 
#> REPORT OF CHECK 2 (saferDev::lambda_check()):
#> INSIDE fun1(), SOME LAMBDA FUNCTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN function():
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 1	\(y)		function(x){ if(x == T) sum(x) else base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \(y){ y * 2 }) }

tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
